senses.definition: Lack of difficulty; the ability to do something easily.
examples: He played the ukelele with ease.
The ease of lifting the weight, despite lack of skill, came from her pure strength.
Her young boy lifted a weight with ease too, as that one wasn't too heavy
The ease with which she passed all the exams surprised her.

senses.definition: Comfort, a state or quality lacking unpleasantness, particularly:

subsenses.definition: Freedom from pain, hardship, and annoyance, sometimes (derogatory, archaic) idleness, sloth.
examples: She enjoyed the ease of living in a house where the servants did all the work.

subsenses.definition: Freedom from worry and concern; peace; sometimes (derogatory, archaic) indifference.
examples: The pension set her mind at ease.

quotes.text: There is ease in the soul of Slid and there be calms upon the sea; also, there be storms upon the sea and troubles in the soul of Slid, for the gods have many moods.
quotes.reference: 1905, Lord Dunsany [i.e., Edward Plunkett, 18th Baron of Dunsany], The Gods of Pegāna, London: [Charles] Elkin Mathews, […], →OCLC, page 16:

examples: We took our ease on the patio.

subsenses.definition: Freedom from financial effort or worry; affluence.
examples: His inheritance catapulted him into a life of ease.

subsenses.definition: Freedom from embarrassment or awkwardness; grace.
examples: She dealt with the faculty with combined authority and ease.

senses.definition: Relief, an end to discomfort, particularly:

subsenses.definition: Followed by of or from: release from or reduction of pain, hardship, or annoyance.
examples: Take one pill every 12 hours to provide ease from pain.

subsenses.definition: (euphemistic, obsolete) Release from intestinal discomfort: defecation.
Release from constraint, obligation, or a constrained position.
(clothing) Additional space provided to allow greater movement.
examples: Add some ease to the waist measurement.

senses.definition: (transitive) To free (something) from pain, worry, agitation, etc.
examples: He eased his conscience by confessing.
